how: Calls recruit participants for building, expanding and reinforcing particular works
Members judge available hands and space inadequate for further commitments
Members revise flag lettering and the position of its name
A timed instruction specifies corresponding pixel placements and repainting the old stripe
A report announces an additional flag beside an existing neighbouring work without establishing an attack
A builder identifies friendly construction being mistaken for damage and undone
The coded choice between giving up and botting supports automation advocacy but requires further evidence before deployment or effectiveness can be asserted
A bare assent accepts a peace proposal without asking anything in return
Members repair lettering, recruit defenders and request coverage while local participants sleep
Neighbour requests produce a flag-shifting counterproposal and a separately accepted peace proposal
A member restores a neighbour's name while another passage asks people to stop converting it
Neighbours trade protection and room, thank collaborators and refuse requests when hands are scarce
Thanks for completing the joint heart support cooperation on a shared mark
Chat invitations support attempted recruitment but require evidence of participation before coalition membership is inferred
Circulating coordination resources and relaying proposals require recognition independently of coalition membership or demonstrated decisions inside external venues
National pride and helping a neighbouring nation's flag give collective identity a local form
Viking history names the target while participants carry on raid talk
Explicit April Fools references frame local joking alongside canvas activity
The AMA and isolated military-service or recent-events titles require contextual evidence before every passage is treated as an April Fools performance
A moderator concentrates canvas discussion in a megathread and announces deletion of individual threads
Participants celebrate completion, thank collaborators and reflect on having held ground together
A request to finish a heart and an adventure title require further evidence before being interpreted as completed-work celebration
Members announce the end and recount the long repair effort
Calls propose raiding and converting other flags without proving that each proposed attack happened
A stop request and an extra-flag report require separation from attack claims despite sharing a broad raiding theme
A complaint receives historical raid banter and a participant's account of abandoning one target for another
Repair, night watch and capacity judgements require separate maintenance and scarcity readings within the flag-design theme
Construction overlapping neighbouring art can initiate negotiation before the maintenance-first sequence has been established
A neighbour's request and a shifting counterproposal make coordinated redesign part of negotiating room for both works
A request to spare neighbouring art receives a request for help moving the flag
Scarce hands can explain refusing additional help rather than relocation
Separate attack and peace proposals require an explicit responsive connection before attack-induced negotiation can be claimed
Seeking defensive support establishes motivation but requires evidence of joining and mutual defence before a completed coalition transition is claimed
Timed coordination and unseen diplomacy channels cannot decide whether canvas leadership or decision rules were formally established
Visible initiative does not identify one original starter whose initial work others joined
Posting a change elsewhere shows relaying but does not establish a person authorised to represent the room
The flag-shifting proposal preserves an existing design and does not establish relocation after erasure
An invitation and a subsequent neighbouring flag leave the host's governing rules unestablished
Historical raiding language does not establish a specific quarrel carried from before the canvas
Peace assent and reciprocal offers do not themselves show disputes about who can bind all placers
The visible agreements do not show a subsequent dispute over representative authority
Dissatisfaction with a final pixel does not show a contest over editing or preserving a shared post-event version
The closing congratulations and reflection do not show a successor canvas or enduring organisational commitment
The closing retrospective leaves the proposed transition from records to durable continuation untested
Personal restoration and treaty assent do not establish that an agreement caused the repair
Repeated repairs and a later bot proposal do not alone establish an implemented maintenance-to-automation transition
Celebrating and recounting coexist without establishing that celebration caused a subsequent preservation effort
The coded bare assent answers a peace proposal rather than a mobilisation call
Recruitment and attack calls coexist without showing that the same recruited hands were redirected
Standalone restraint and later repair do not directly answer the coded attack calls
Calls and the moderation instruction establish both practices but do not themselves establish the proposed flood mechanism
